newsitem.title: USA: Senate support growing for DC tax cut--panel chair.
newsitem.headline: Senate support growing for DC tax cut--panel chair.

text.p: Support is growing in the U.S. Senate for cutting the capital gains tax in the District of Columbia instead of President Clinton's plan for a White House-controlled economic development corporation for the city, the chairman of a key Senate panel said Tuesday.

"Don't you think if we would just lower or zero the capital gains on real property in the District versus, you would attract far more growth and economic opportunity for D.C.?" Sen. Sam Brownback, chairman of the Senate Government Affairs panel on D.C.
